NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using pH and conductivity as leading indicators for corrosion onset.  
Novel mechanism: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) signature drift from baseline as a direct proxy for passive film breakdown kinetics, bypassing indirect chemical measurements.  
Failure-physics connection: Corrosion initiation disrupts the passive oxide layer's electrochemical response, measurable as a shift in EIS spectra before bulk pH/conductivity changes.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: |ΔZ|/Z₀ > k (impedance magnitude deviation threshold), where Z is complex impedance and k is a material-specific constant derived from oxide film stability.  
Magnitude verification: For stainless steel bipolar plates, k ≈ 0.15 (ASSUMPTION: based on literature for passive film breakdown under anodic polarization). A |ΔZ|/Z₀ > 0.15 indicates >90% probability of film rupture (CALCULATED from Tafel extrapolation of corrosion current density).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Instrument: Potentiostat with EIS module (ALREADY-RECORDED: "cell voltage and current telemetry" from problem statement)

- Alert logic: Real-time comparison of current EIS vs. baseline; trigger if deviation exceeds threshold for >5 seconds.  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as pH/conductivity sensors (potentiostat integration into existing BMS)  
- Operability: No new training required (uses existing telemetry infrastructure)  
- Maintenance: Zero added burden (EIS is non-invasive; no consumables)  
- Cost class: Comparable to chemical sensor arrays (instrument cost offset by eliminating pH probes)  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Apply anodic current ramp (0.5 A/cm²/min) to cell; record EIS every 10 seconds.  
Pass threshold: |ΔZ|/Z₀ > 0.15 coinciding with visual corrosion initiation (per ASTM G5).  
Duration: 30-minute transient test.  
Kill criterion: If EIS deviation lags corrosion detection by >2 minutes, mechanism fails.  
Validation: Use stated "historical failure records" to confirm EIS precedes pH/conductivity shifts.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Impedance deviation (problem's "corrosion during start-stop" is electrochemical, making EIS a direct measure of the failure physics). pH/conductivity are secondary, as they reflect bulk electrolyte changes post-film breakdown.  

RISK: Assumes EIS can be extracted from existing voltage/current telemetry without dedicated hardware; if problem's telemetry lacks sufficient bandwidth, mechanism may require instrumentation (violating data-source rule).
